audit.whatIsWrong: All seven full-layer sides read 'Skill' while win[] reads LeBlanc, LeBlanc, LeBlanc, LeBlanc, Zed, Zed, Zed.
audit.why: packet.levelChart matches the content layer exactly, so the full layer is the stale copy and the page answers 'who wins Level 6' two different ways.
audit.corrected: Sides aligned to the packet as one atomic group, and phases[4].why, [5].why and [6].why rewritten so the three Zed stages no longer carry sentences describing LeBlanc winning them.

audit.why: The Eclipse-first-item flip and the Edge of Night three-item spike are both consistent with the chart handing Zed stages 5, 6 and 7, and with the 51.37% win rate over 4028 games. Spike timings left as they are.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive property of Death Mark was never stated: Zed is untargetable for the dash and the mark pays out 3 seconds later.
audit.why: Riot's R text is explicit — 'Zed becomes untargetable and dashes to an enemy champion, marking them. After 3 seconds the mark triggers.' That untargetability is what eats a LeBlanc commit, and the 3-second delay is the exact window your Distortion return or Mimic has to leave in. The page instead said 'spend your defensive answer AFTER the mark lands' with no number and no mention of untargetability.
audit.corrected: Stated in breakdown.cooldowns, enemyWin, phases[4].why, phases[5].why and spikes[3].

audit.whatIsWrong: The page credited Zed with 'reset potential' — an ultimate reset off a kill — in whys[6], wants.foe[2] and the late paragraph, and called Living Shadow a stealth tool.
audit.why: Riot's Death Mark text contains no reset condition of any kind, and Living Shadow is a shadow swap on 20/19/18/17/16s, not stealth. Both were inventions.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the real mechanics: the untargetable entry, the 3-second mark, and the swap as his only escape.

edits.before: Mimic online — the double-dash crosses the lane and the burst doubles. Most mids die to the first full chain.
edits.after: Death Mark goes untargetable for the dash and detonates 3 seconds later — your burst has nowhere to land inside it.

edits.before: First item spike: Q-W-RW deletes squishies. Spend the lane lead before scaling lanes wake.
edits.after: His first item turns the 3-second Death Mark into a kill. Never be inside 625 range while it is up.

edits.before: Late LeBlanc picks: W the flank, chain the carry, mimic the exit — and vanish before the obituary prints.
edits.after: He picks first now: Living Shadow on 16s gives him two angles, and Death Mark eats your commit outright.

edits.before: - Zed Death Mark: matchup-defining — The all-in — spend your defensive answer AFTER the mark lands, not before. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Distortion (return) like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Death Mark (R): 120s at rank 1 — untargetable through the dash, and the mark pays out 3 seconds later. Spend your answer after it lands. - Living Shadow (W) is 20s at rank 1: the swap is his only exit. - Shadow Slash (E) is 5s.

edits.before: Q the sigil, W the detonation, return before the answer — a half-bar round trip he experienced as weather.
edits.after: Once Living Shadow is spent he has 20 seconds with no swap — chain him there and he eats the whole rotation.

edits.before: Zed burns Death Mark on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Mimic Distortion is your exit from a 3-second mark — save it for that.

edits.before: That is Zed’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Shadow Slash is 290 range on a 5-second cooldown and slows — that is his floor.

edits.before: Staying at the W landing spot for one more auto — the return timer is your champion; outliving it is optional.
edits.after: He refunds energy whenever he and a shadow hit the same target — at even health his resource outlasts yours.

edits.before: Zed wins by landing Death Mark, denying your pattern, and cashing the all-in before your pattern matures.
edits.after: Zed wins by going untargetable through your burst with Death Mark and cashing the mark three seconds later.

edits.before: Carry through picks — one chained carry per objective; your job is the flank angle and the discipline to leave after.
edits.after: Carry through picks — chain him after Living Shadow is spent; 20 seconds without the swap is the only time he cannot leave.

edits.before: If Zed gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Death Mark extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with W clears and stay relevant through chain picks.
edits.after: If Zed gets a kill, stop standing inside 625 range while his ultimate is up and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling — W-clear, hold Distortion for the mark, and take your picks off-lane.

edits.before: Zed's fully itemized burst, spellshield, and reset potential make him the dominant pick-threat once both are fully built.
edits.after: Zed's fully itemized burst, Edge of Night spellshield, and untargetable Death Mark entry make him the dominant pick-threat late.

edits.before: A fed Zed with Death Mark burst and spellshield from Edge of Night can blow past LeBlanc's combo and delete her from the fog of Living Shadow.
edits.after: A fed Zed with an Edge of Night spellshield eats your chain, then goes untargetable through your answer on a 100-second Death Mark.

edits.before: With a scaled build including Edge of Night for spellshield-protected engages and Lord Dominik's for armor penetration, Zed becomes a terrifying pick threat who can bypass LeBlanc's chains, burst her from stealth via Living Shadow, and reset off the kill to escape unpunished. LeBlanc's combo is telegraphed and squishy, giving Zed every advantage in a prolonged 1v1 or pick scenario. This makes Zed the clear favorite once both champions are fully itemized.
edits.after: With a scaled build including Edge of Night for spellshield-protected engages and Lord Dominik's for armor penetration, Zed becomes a terrifying pick threat who eats your chain behind the shield, opens from fog with a Living Shadow swap, and goes untargetable through your answer with Death Mark. Your combo is telegraphed and squishy, giving Zed every advantage in a prolonged 1v1 or pick scenario. This makes Zed the clear favorite once both champions are fully itemized.

notes: CHART: all seven rows disagreed across layers; packet.levelChart matches content win[] exactly, so the full-layer sides were moved onto it as one atomic group and the three now-Zed stages had their why rewritten in the same proposal. No paired win[N] edits exist because the content values are already correct (a no-op edit is not proposable) — after this lands both layers agree on all seven rows. Ratings untouched: the rating perspective is inconsistent across this champion's pages and guessing would inject a new error (same question logged on yasuo). CONTENT-INTERNAL CONFLICT LEFT ALONE AND FLAGGED: content whys[2] and spikes[1] both say LeBlanc still out-bursts Zed at level 6, while win[4] and the packet hand Level 6 to Zed. The whys[] array on this matchup does not map 1:1 to the seven chart rows (whys[1] covers levels 3-5), so I could not tell which stage whys[2] is meant to describe and did not touch it. This page is also written in third person ('LeBlanc should shove...') rather than the second-person voice used everywhere else; converting it would be a full-page rewrite outside this pass's scope, so it is reported rather than done.
